IS : 10097 - 1982 

Indian Standard 

CODE OF 
PRACTICE FOR THE PACKAGING OF 

METAL CUTTING TOOLS 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 26 February 1982, after the diaft finalized by the 
Packaging of Engineering Goods Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division 
Council. 

0.2 Metal cutting tools are fragile tools and the impacts in transport- 
ation may render them absolutely useless. Therefore, thejr packaging for 
transportation requires special attention The material required for 
packaging to meet this specific requirement would help both manufac** 
turers as well as the users of these tools. 

0.3 The cutting edge of the tools is most important requiring protection 
and corrosion is a significant factor to be prevented during transportation 
and storage. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This code of practice lays down guidelines for the packaging of 
metal cutting tools. 

2. REQUIREMENTS 

2.1 Before packing the tools shall be given a rust prevention for normal 
storage conditions. This may be by: 

a) Strippable coating, 

b) Oil, 

c) Vapour phase inhibitor, and 

d) Waxed paper. 



IS : 10097 - 1982 

2.2 In a smgle packing unit tools of the same designation and quality 
characteristics shall be packed. 

2.3 A common bigger container may be used for a number of primary- 
pack units provided these units can be identified easily by means of their 
labels or packs. 

2.4 External dimensions of the transport package where possible shall 
conform to IS : 8470-1977* to permit unitization for easy handling in 
transportation. 

2.5 The transport packages shall be packed with cushioning materia] so 
as to prevent rattling of the products inside the case and to minimise the 
damage to the contents during transportation. 

2.6 The inner surface of the transport package shall have a lining of 
one oT the water proof materials, like paper laminated with bitumen, 
plastic, etc, or polyethylene sheets. 

2.7 Materials — Recommended materials for cushioning and transport 
packs are given in Table 1. 

2.8 The gross mass of transport container shall not exceed 80 kg, 
3. MARKING 

3.1 The transport pack shall be marked with the following: 

*- - a) Symbol for 'Handling with Care' [ see IS: 12G0 (Part II)- 
lD79t],and 

b) Gross mass. 



•Dimensiorib of rigid rectangular transport packages.

General (roads f second revision 1.
